## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: will UODO publish a news item naming FELG / FELG Dent by 16 Oct 2026? (compiled 2026-10-05)

## 1. What the resolution source shows now (https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/138, fetched 2026-10-05)
- **Not resolved yet:** none of the 20 most recent items (17.09–05.10.2026) names FELG, FELG Dent or FELG Software, or mentions a leak from dental practices.
- **Newest items on the page:**
  - 05.10.2026: "Kara pieniężna nałożona za niewykonanie decyzji Prezesa UODO" (/pl/138/4594)
  - 01.10.2026: seminar report with ZUS (/pl/531/4592)
  - 30.09.2026: "Prezes UODO interweniuje w sprawie danych osobowych w systemach aptecznych" (/pl/138/4591). This is about pharmacy systems and wholesalers Neuca, Farmacol and PGF, not FELG.
- **UODO's own search** (https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/search?query=FELG) returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-05. A web search for "site:uodo.gov.pl FELG" found nothing, and no media article quotes UODO on FELG.
- **Uncertain:** item ID 4593 was missing from the list. Titles were read through a summarising fetch tool, so the wording may differ slightly.
- **Similar recent case on the same page:** 25.09.2026, "Miliony Polaków poszkodowane. Po nowym wycieku danych medycznych PUODO zapowiada kontrolę" (/pl/138/4585). It names Medyc and Qbusoft and announces an inspection.

## 2. FELG Dent incident: timeline and current status
- **~6 or 9 Sept 2026: attack starts.** Data was pulled through an API flaw (IDOR) that let a demo account reach production data from other clients. Sources disagree on the date: zaufanatrzeciastrona.pl and cyberscope.pl say 6 Sept, niebezpiecznik.pl says 9 Sept.
- **28 Sept, ~18:00: FELG detects the breach.**
- **29 Sept: extortion begins.**
- **1 Oct 2026, evening: becomes public.** An attacker calling themselves "Horus" contacted Sekurak, Niebezpiecznik and Zaufana Trzecia Strona; Sekurak's article went up at 19:53.
  - https://sekurak.pl/wyciek-incydent-bezpieczenstwa-w-felg-gabinety-dentystyczne-atakujacy-twierdza-ze-uzyskali-dostep-do-ponad-dwoch-milionow-rekordow-z-danymi-pacjentow/
  - https://cyberscope.pl/2026/10/01/mozliwy-kolejny-duzy-wyciek-danych-medycznych-mowa-o-24-mln-pacjentow/
- **2 Oct: FELG confirms the attack and a 100,000 PLN ransom demand.** The CEO later said there was no direct demand, which contradicts this, so treat it as uncertain.
  - https://www.rmf24.pl/fakty/polska/news-kolejny-wyciek-danych-medycznych-sprawca-ataku-zada-okupu,nIdn,1020239
  - https://www.rp.pl/spoleczenstwo/art45239351-wyciek-danych-pacjentow-z-oprogramowania-dla-stomatologow-w-tle-szantaz-i-zadanie-okupu (updated 5 Oct)
- **Scale (no figure is confirmed):**
  - The attacker claims 2.4M patient records, 712k staff records and 1.2M prescriptions.
  - FELG says about 2M patient records and about 28k staff.
  - FELG overall serves over 4,000 clinics and about 12M patient cards (infodent24).
- **FELG and UODO:** FELG says it "contacted" UODO and filed a criminal complaint with the prosecutor's office.
  - It asked clinics to wait before filing their own reports to UODO. Media called this legally risky, because clinics are the data controllers and have 72 hours to report (dentonet, infodent24, rp.pl).
  - It promised clinics a ready-made UODO notification and a patient-notification tool "in the coming days".
  - https://dentonet.pl/lekarz/mozliwy-wyciek-danych-pacjentow-z-systemu-felg-dent-firma-potwierdza-cyberatak
  - https://www.infodent24.pl/newsdentpost/cyberatak-na-felg-dent-nawet-2-mln-rekordow-pacjentow-moglo-wyciec-z-gabinetow,128035.html
- **Government side:**
  - Deputy PM and Digital Affairs Minister Gawkowski (about 2–5 Oct) warned firms they "will be held responsible" and announced plans for mandatory audits or certification (Interia, spidersweb 2 Oct).
  - Centrum e-Zdrowia and its incident team CSIRT CeZ are monitoring the case (RMF24).
  - A CERT Polska statement is not confirmed.
- **Context:** this follows MyDr (August, about 19M people), Medyc/Qbusoft (24 Sept), Enel-Med (24–27 Sept) and Fakturownia (27–28 Sept). It is also before the question window: on 16.09.2026 the UODO President broadened health-sector inspections.
- **Scheduled events before 16 Oct:** none found, apart from FELG's promised notifications.

## 3. Base rates: UODO news items naming a company after a publicised breach
- **Big, nationally covered medical breaches since 2023:** about 4 of 4 got a named UODO item quickly.

| Incident | Became public | UODO named item | Lag |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALAB | about 21–23.11.2023 | 30.11.2023, https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/138/2920 | about 7–9 days |
| DCG Centrum Medyczne | patients told 25.03.2024 | 28.03.2024, https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/138/3047 | about 3 days |
| MyDr | 12.08.2026 | 12.08.2026, /pl/138/4539; 13.08 "Prezes UODO skontroluje spółkę MyDr", /pl/138/4540 | 0–1 days |
| Medyc/Qbusoft | media about 24–25.09.2026 | 25.09.2026, /pl/138/4585 | 0–1 days |

- **Other breaches:**
  - Pandabuy got a named item after 32 days: 02.05.2024, /pl/138/3082.
  - Morele.net (2018), mBank, Santander and others were named only at the fine or court stage, months to years later.
  - Recent non-medical breaches have no named item yet as of 05.10.2026: Fakturownia (27–28.09) and Wakacje.pl (29.09).
  - Enel-Med (24–27.09) also has no separate UODO item. It may be covered inside the Medyc item 4585; this is not confirmed.
- **Typical wording of quick items:** "Prezes UODO skontroluje spółkę X" (will inspect company X) or "Prezes UODO monitoruje sprawę wycieku…" (is monitoring the leak). They usually advise people to check bezpiecznedane.gov.pl and to block (zastrzec) their PESEL number.
- **How FELG compares:** 4 days after it went public (1 Oct to 5 Oct), FELG has no UODO item. That is already slower than MyDr and Medyc, but within the ALAB lag of about 9 days.
- **Possible explanation (my inference, unverified):** UODO may be waiting for formal breach notifications from clinics, which FELG asked them to delay.
- **Not checked:** whether any UODO item names a vendor rather than the clinic (FELG is a software supplier). Qbusoft and MyDr are precedents where UODO named the vendor.

## 4. Prediction markets
- None found.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, as of 23:59 UTC on October 15, 2026, the Polish Personal Data Protection Office (UODO) "Aktualności" (news) section at https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/138 contains at least one announcement that explicitly names "FELG" (e.g. FELG Dent or FELG Software) in the context of the September/October 2026 data breach of the FELG Dent dental practice management system. The announcement must be dated on or after January 1, 2026 and must refer to the FELG/FELG Dent incident by name; a general statement about medical-sector data leaks or planned inspections that does not name FELG does not count. Otherwise the question resolves NO.
letra_pequena: A match may be identified via the UODO news page's search function or by browsing the dated list of articles. If uodo.gov.pl is temporarily unreachable on the resolution date, resolution waits until it is accessible again. If the specific URL changes, the equivalent official UODO news/announcements index on uodo.gov.pl is used. A dedicated statement, press release, or news article published by UODO that names FELG/FELG Dent counts; a mere entry in UODO's register of reported breaches, or coverage by third-party media alone, does not count unless reproduced as a UODO news-section announcement.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, until 23:59 UTC on October 15, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. As of October 5, no qualifying UODO news announcement has been found.

(c) **Reference class:** The research identifies four prominent medical-data breaches since 2023 that received a prompt, named UODO news item—4 of 4. That is a small, potentially selective sample; some other recent breaches have not received one.

(d) **NO scenario:** UODO handles FELG through notifications or inspections but publishes only general health-sector updates before the deadline.

(e) **YES scenario:** UODO posts a short update naming FELG Dent while describing its monitoring or inspection of the breach.

(f) **Deciding technicality:** The item must appear in UODO’s official *Aktualności* section by **October 15 at 23:59 UTC** and explicitly name FELG in connection with this breach. A generic warning or third-party article does not count.

The medical-breach precedent favors YES, but the absence of an item four days after the incident became public—and UODO’s option to address it without a dedicated announcement—keeps me short of high confidence.

Probability: 62%

(c) **Reference class:** The research identifies four recent, prominent medical-data breaches that received a named UODO news item within roughly nine days. That is an encouraging 4/4 precedent, though it is a small sample, and other recent breaches have not received separate items.

(d) **NO scenario:** UODO handles FELG through notifications or inspections but publishes only general health-sector updates—or waits until after the deadline to name it.

(e) **YES scenario:** UODO publishes a short update saying it is monitoring or investigating the FELG Dent breach.

(f) **Decisive technicality:** An item must **explicitly name FELG** in UODO’s *Aktualności* section by the October 15 UTC cutoff. A general warning, third-party report, or breach-register entry does not count.

The scale of the breach and the medical-sector precedents favor YES. The lack of an item so far weighs against it, but the incident became public only on October 1, leaving relatively little working time for UODO to respond.

Probability: 70%

(a) **Time left:** about 10 days, from 5 October to 23:59 UTC on 15 October 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** No. As of 5 October, none of the 20 most recent UODO news items names FELG, FELG Dent or FELG Software.

(c) **Reference class:**
- Every big, nationally covered medical breach since 2023 (ALAB, DCG, MyDr, Medyc/Qbusoft) got a UODO news item naming the company. The lag was 0–9 days, and the two 2026 cases appeared within 1 day.
- Non-medical breaches the same week (Fakturownia, Wakacje.pl) got nothing.
- FELG is already 4 days past disclosure with no item. That is slower than the 2026 pattern, though still within ALAB's lag.

(d) **No scenario:**
- UODO now treats the wave of breaches through general health-sector inspection statements and does not name each new incident.
- It may also wait for formal notifications from the clinics (FELG asked them to delay) and handle FELG quietly through proceedings.
- Its news output stays on fines, seminars and general guidance until after 15 October.

(e) **Yes scenario:**
- Clinic breach notifications flood into UODO, and the minister's statements keep up public pressure.
- UODO then publishes something like "Prezes UODO skontroluje FELG" or "monitoruje wyciek z FELG Dent". A Yes could also come from guidance reminding dental practices that they are the data controllers and must report within 72 hours, naming FELG.
- UODO has already named vendors directly (Qbusoft, MyDr), so naming the supplier rather than the clinics has precedent.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- The item must explicitly name FELG and appear in the Aktualności news section; an entry in the breach register or third-party media coverage does not count.
- A general dental-sector or medical-sector statement without the name does not count.
- UODO's site search was returning errors, but browsing the dated list of articles is also accepted for resolution.
- Item ID 4593 was missing from the list, which is a small chance something was missed.

**Overall:** The strong base rate for large medical breaches pulls toward Yes. Against that, 4 days of silence while UODO is clearly busy, plus its silence on Fakturownia and Wakacje.pl, suggests it may have switched to general statements. The controller-obligation angle (clinics told to delay their 72-hour reports) gives UODO a natural reason to comment by name.

Probability: 42%
